root.name: Torre Attack: Wagner Gambit
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Nf3 e6 3. Bg5 c5 4. e4

overview: White plays 4.e4 against the Torre set-up, offering the central pawn to open lines. Black can take on d4 or e4 and keep a pawn, while White hopes for a lead in development and pressure on the Black king. The play is open and forcing, and the line is a rare side road from the usual Torre structure.

white_ideas.idea: Open the centre with e4 for piece play
Use Bg5 and the d-file to pressure the Black position

black_ideas.idea: Take on d4 or e4 and keep the pawn

character.notes: A pawn offered for activity opens the position at once.

gambit.notes: Black can take on d4 or e4 and keep the pawn.

structure.notes: The d- and e-pawns are exchanged, opening the centre.

approach.notes: A gambit that strong players seldom choose.

character.reason: A pawn offer and open lines make the play forcing.

gambit.reason: White offers a pawn that Black can keep.

soundness.reason: Compensation for the pawn is questionable.

structure.reason: Central pawns come off and lines open.

level.reason: A Dubious line is never Beginner.

plans.reason: The gambit aims for faster piece activity.
